stem: An insulin-treated adult has an uncertain diabetes classification, and the clinician orders a serum C-peptide level. What information can this test contribute?

options.A: It estimates average glycemia over several months and therefore provides the same information as hemoglobin A1c testing.
options.B: It can help assess residual endogenous insulin secretory reserve and should be interpreted with the clinical context and other diagnostic information.
options.C: It determines diabetes type independently of clinical history, renal function, insulin use, and other laboratory findings.
options.D: It primarily measures glomerular filtration and does not provide useful information about endogenous pancreatic insulin secretion.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance lists serum C-peptide testing as useful for assessing insulin secretory reserve in selected diabetic patients who are receiving insulin therapy, including assessment of residual endogenous insulin secretory reserve. C-peptide is cosecreted with endogenous insulin and is mainly removed by the kidneys, so renal failure and other clinical factors can affect interpretation. B is therefore correct. A confuses C-peptide with long-term glycemic markers, C overstates the test as an independent diabetes classifier, and D incorrectly assigns renal filtration as its primary diagnostic purpose.
educational_objective: Use C-peptide as supportive information about residual endogenous insulin secretion in selected insulin-treated patients while integrating clinical history and other diagnostic data.
source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories Test Catalog; test definition generated May/June 2026; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Useful For: assessing insulin secretory reserve in selected diabetic patients receiving insulin therapy, including residual endogenous insulin secretory reserve. Clinical Information: C-peptide is cosecreted with insulin and mainly removed by kidneys; kidney failure and other conditions alter levels.
source_claim_supported: Serum C-peptide can help assess residual endogenous insulin secretory reserve in selected insulin-treated diabetic patients but requires clinical-context interpretation.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor diagnostic-test results, perform focused assessments, and integrate findings with client condition.
correction_summary: Balanced all options and retained C-peptide as supportive evidence of endogenous insulin secretion rather than an independent diabetes classifier.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — Mayo explicitly supports residual insulin-secretory-reserve assessment in insulin-treated patients and identifies renal influences; B is appropriately qualified and uniquely best.
